payload.first_observation:
[environment] workspace files: ENVIRONMENT.json (policy, tasks, budget, constraints), STATUS.json (current state, rewritten after every command), SCOREBOARD.md (dev scores, lineage)
[environment] facts: tasks [nut, restack, revstack]; budget 16 GPU-h; mode dev; adapter_mode library
[environment] briefing (facts from ENVIRONMENT.json, tasks.json, SCOREBOARD.md, the trainer doc and the tool scripts; full docs: skills/tools/SKILL.md, skills/trainer/SKILL.md, tasks/<name>.md):
[environment] evaluation: The one adapter stack you submit serves every task at the hidden evaluation. The final score is the total number of successes of the submitted policy on the hidden evaluation, summed over its tasks; dev-seed evals (eval.py) never count toward it. The hidden evaluation runs on hidden seeds you never see, and also on unlisted variants of the listed task families. tasks.json lists every task you can train and dev-evaluate; tasks/<name>.md holds each task's full Goal text from its eval prompt. One stack serves every task at the hidden evaluation, so a gain on one task can cost successes on another, and a gain that holds only on seeds you practised on does not carry over.
[environment] metric: Total hidden-seed successes across all tasks of the scored policy (finish.py: the submitted one, by default the loaded stack).
[environment] tasks overview: robot: A Franka Emika robot arm in CaP-X Robosuite simulation, driven through the perception and control APIs listed in each task's eval prompt (CaP-X API tier s4). program: Per trial the policy writes one single-turn Python program: executable code only, comments allowed, no code fences. success: Each task's own success check. evaluation: Hidden seeds; the one adapter stack you submit serves every task.
[environment] family pick-and-place, example restack: Goal: Gently place the red cube on top of the green cube and then open the gripper. Nothing should be dropped from a height. / Use the extent of the cubes to calculate the exact height for placement.
[environment]   Tasks sharing this form, each differing in: revstack: Pick up the green cube and gently stack it on top of the red cube, then release it.
[environment] family nut-assembly, example nut: Goal: grasp and insert the `brown square nut` onto the `brown square block`. / Note that you would grasp the nut by its handle. You can try language query `extruded handle of the brown square nut` to get a good grasp at the handle. / The brown square nut and the extruded handle of the brown square nut are part of the same rigid body. / The grasp pose query for 'extruded handle of the brown square nut' returns an end-effector pose expressed in world frame, located on the handle region. / The nut's object center pose obtained via 'white hollow center of the brown square nut' and the handle grasp pose obtained via 'extruded handle of the brown square nut' have a fixed rigid transform, which must be applied correctly when inserting the nut onto the peg.
[environment] base dev counts (SCOREBOARD.md base column): not recorded
[environment] train spec fields (field=default): task=this session's task set (see Defaults), name=a<job id>, steps=as many as your remaining budget affords (see Defaults), batch=8 (a task list: the smallest batch >= 8 that splits as asked), weights=none: an equal split, rollouts=8, lr=2e-5, init=none: the adapter this session trained last is continued natively (none yet: a fresh LoRA); see Continuation, init_mode=none (see `init`), start_preset=none, start_mix=none, reward=task_completed, seed_start=the lineage's next unused block (`seed_cursor`): the first call of a lineage (no `init`) starts at 810001; a continuation (`init`) starts right after the seeds its lineage has used (`seeds_consumed` in each `adapters/<name>/call.json`); set it to replay seeds, seeds=none (`seed_start` applies), note=none, goal=none, time=set by the site: 1 GPU 25 min + 13 min x steps, 2 GPUs 85 min + 17 min x steps, 3 GPUs 30 min + 14 min x steps, at least 2 h (whole minutes, rounded up; the job record's `config` shows the value used), data=none, objective=grpo, epochs=1, min_reward=1.0, stop_when=none (all `steps` run)
[environment] cost (GPU-h; Admission reserves the site's cost estimate; each call is charged the site's cost per call (skills/trainer/SKILL.md, Cost) on completion; gpu_hours_actual is measured time, not charged.): call: canonical cost; train, 1 step: 0.39; train, 10 steps: 1.98; train, 30 steps: 5.50; train, 10 steps, `rollouts` 16: 3.74; train, N steps: 2 x (0.1079 + 0.0881 x N x batch / 8 x rollouts / 8); eval of one task on: 5 seeds | 20 seeds | 100 seeds; canonical cost: 0.15 | 0.19 | 0.45
[environment] a train produces: A finished train writes `adapters/<name>/` (read-only to you): `adapter_model.safetensors`, `adapter_config.json`, `rewards.json` (per step: `step`, `score_mean` over that step's rollouts), `call.json` (job ids, `gpu_hours` = the canonical charge to your budget, `gpu_hours_actual` = measured hardware time, not charged, nonzero LoRA-B count, rollout seed range) and `training.json` (`resolved_spec`: the controls actually used). The adapter can then be named in `eval.py --adapter`, `load.py`, or as `init` of another train.
[environment] option: Training data (`data`): `data` names a JSONL file in your workspace (a path relative to the workspace, or absolute inside it): one line per training prompt, `{"task": ..., "seed": ..., "variant": ..., "prompt": ...}` (`variant` and `prompt` optional, no other keys):
[environment] option: SFT (`objective: sft`): A spec `{"objective": "sft", "data": "<file>.jsonl"}` (optional: `name`, `init`, `epochs` (1), `batch` (16 rows per step), `lr` (1e-4), `min_reward` (1.0), `time`; no other field) trains the policy's LoRA by supervised fine-tuning (cross-entropy on the program's tokens only; LoRA rank 32 / alpha 64 on the policy's modules, or `init` continued; without `init` it continues the policy's own init, as a practice call does).
[environment] train objectives for this session's policy (Qwen3.8-27B): grpo, sft; sft trains on Tinker (an init adapter must be one trained on Tinker)
[environment] tools:
[environment]   python3 train.py SPEC -- train an adapter from your spec file (JSON or YAML; any keys).
[environment]   python3 eval.py --adapter A[,B...]|base|loaded --task T --seeds N [--reward FILE] -- success count of that adapter stack on N fresh dev seeds.
[environment]   python3 load.py load A [B...] | stack A [B...] | unload [A...] -- set, extend or shrink the adapter stack on your own serving endpoint (unload with no names = base).
[environment]   python3 wait.py all | ID [ID...] [--max DURATION] -- after this command, block until those jobs finish before your next turn, at most DURATION (hours or minutes: 4h, 90m; default 2h).
[environment]   python3 status.py [ID...] -- print the state and result of jobs (all jobs if no ID), then what finishing now would score.
[environment]   python3 cancel.py ID -- stop a running train or eval job.
[environment]   python3 finish.py [--policy base | --adapters A[@VERSION][,B...]] [--note TEXT]  |  python3 finish.py --confirm TOKEN -- End the session in two steps.
[environment]   python3 rollout.py --adapter A[,B...]|base|loaded --task T --seeds N [--reward FILE] -- run the policy (that adapter stack) on N fresh dev seeds of task T and return, per seed, its program, the tail of what the program printed and the run facts (seed, sandbox_rc, secs, wall_s, task), plus task_completed and stdout_tail on a task whose verifier you can see, and there, where the site runs the programs on the task's practice simulator, sim_reward, stages and final_state.
[environment]   python3 preset.py --task T --name NAME ( --program FILE --seeds N | --from rollouts/<job>.jsonl --where "<predicate over r>" ) -- Build start states for practice on task T, saved per source seed and kept only if every state restores.
